title: All Happy Companies Are Different
coreMove: Look for the structural difference that lets a company escape direct comparison.
sourcePressure: The chapter contrasts monopoly-created uniqueness with competitive sameness, arguing that direct rivalry erodes profits and narrows strategic imagination.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Saying monopoly is always good or competition is always bad as a moral claim.

sourceAnchors.name: Tolstoy
sourceAnchors.detail: the source sidecar lists Tolstoy as a proper noun tied to the chapter title allusion
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Like the old line about unhappy families, weak companies start to resemble one another when the fight compresses them.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.audience: an operations VP comparing another price war route with an underserved medical travel corridor
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the airline bleeds margin or owns a route others cannot easily compare
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: James removes the competitor fare column and marks the corridor where comparison breaks
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a route map with one red string crossing the north coast

exampleSpecs.audience: a product lead deciding whether to chase every rival feature or own one compliance workflow completely
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the company becomes a checklist clone with thin margins
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Camille asks which feature would make procurement stop comparing line items
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a procurement matrix projected too large on the wall

exampleSpecs.audience: a founder choosing between commodity lettuce and rare winter herbs for restaurants
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the co-op competes on price or creates a small monopoly around supply reliability
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Michael watches chefs ignore the lettuce sample and fight for the winter basil tray

exampleSpecs.audience: a founder deciding whether to serve every clinic or specialize in one painful oncology billing code set
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether specialization creates uniqueness or general service traps the firm in price comparison
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chloe circles the oncology denial queue and writes different enough to matter
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a denial queue printed across six pages

exampleSpecs.audience: a creative director choosing between a trend clone and a strange mechanic only their team can execute
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the studio gets compared into oblivion or earns its own category
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Niklas cuts the familiar combat demo and lets testers play only the odd mechanic
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a controller cable coiled under a playtest table

exampleSpecs.audience: a partner deciding whether to join a crowded contract market or own cross-border art restitution work
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the firm keeps billable hours but loses strategic distinction
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Paula reviews last year’s crowded RFP losses and moves the team toward the one rare case type
exampleSpecs.firstImage: archival photos spread across a legal table
